This is the Halara Coffee Club Point of Sale and Inventory System: an Android tablet app for the staff, and a web dashboard for the admin.
Part one: the staff app on the Android tablet.
Staff sign in with their own account. Here we use the demo credentials.
The home screen shows today's sales, transactions, and low-stock alerts.
Before taking orders, the cashier must open a shift, so every payment is traceable.
The cashier enters the starting cash, one thousand pesos, and opens the shift.
Each menu item shows its price, and how many servings can still be made from the ingredients in stock.
When an ingredient runs out, like the ham for this sandwich, the item is disabled automatically.
Staff filter by category, and tap plus to add items to the order.
In the cart, quantities can be adjusted.
Cash, G-Cash, and Maya are supported. For cash, quick-amount buttons compute the change instantly.
Once confirmed, the sale is saved, recipe ingredients are deducted from inventory, and the receipt prints directly to the Bluetooth printer.
For G-Cash or Maya, the store's QR code is shown. The cashier confirms only after the payment arrives.
The Orders screen lists every transaction, where receipts can be reprinted, and orders refunded.
Staff can also check raw material stock, with low and out-of-stock labels.
At the end of the shift, the cashier counts the drawer and closes the shift. The system records any difference from the expected cash.
Part two: the admin dashboard on the web.
On the web, users choose their role. Only admin accounts can open the admin side.
The dashboard summarizes sales, transactions, stock alerts, and products. The tablet orders we just made already appear here, in real time.
Low-stock and out-of-stock notifications are created automatically.
The Sales page lets the admin search transactions, view receipts, export to CSV, and refund orders.
In Products, each menu item has a recipe per serving. This links every sale to the inventory.
Raw materials are tracked in grams, milliliters, or pieces, each with its own low-stock level.
When a delivery arrives, the admin records the quantity and purchase cost. Here, five liters of oat milk.
Stock updates immediately, the alert clears, and a weighted-average cost values the inventory.
Cash Management shows every cashier shift, with the expected cash, counted cash, and variance.
Reports show daily revenue, top-selling products, and the payment method mix.
The inventory report covers stock value, deliveries, ingredient usage, and alerts. Both reports export to PDF or CSV.
In Settings, the admin manages their profile and password, and uploads the G-Cash and Maya QR codes used by the tablet.
In summary: Cash, G-Cash and Maya payments, automatic recipe-based inventory, low-stock alerts, shift reconciliation, exportable reports, and Bluetooth receipt printing. Thank you!
